Char: Participants:
260 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Iran.

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 years or older with a gestational age of 38 to 42 weeks and a singleton pregnancy who had request for elective termination of pregnancy before 42 weeks of gestation or had medical indication for labor induction (hypertension and diabetes). Additional criteria for enrollment were birth weight of maximally 4,000 grams, normal fetal heart rate, cephalic presentation, lack of uterine contractures, and Bishop’s score of 6 or less.

Exclusion criteria: lack of satisfaction for incorporation in the study, a positive history of uterine surgery including cesarean, intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR), oligohydramnios, placenta previa, umbilical cord prolapse, active herpes infection, symptoms of chorioamnionitis, hepatic or renal disease, non-reactive contraindications for prostaglandins use, contraindications for labour induction, and idiopathic vaginal bleeding.
Char: Interventions: 25 µg oral misoprostol vs. oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
210 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Nigeria.

Inclusion criteria: women with live singleton fetuses with cephalic presentation, intact membranes, reactive nonstress test, and unfavourable cervices (Bishop’s score < 6) scheduled to undergo induction of labour at term.

Exclusion criteria: women with pregnancies < 37 weeks’ gestation, intrauterine fetal death, multiple gestations, previous uterine surgery, prelabour rupture of fetal membranes, abnormal nonstress test and any contraindication to vaginal delivery were excluded. Also, women who did not give their consent or have prenatal care in this centre were excluded.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Balloon catheters plus < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: women at term (37 weeks of gestation or greater) with a singleton fetus, cephalic presentation, and a Bishop score of 6 or less.

Exclusion criteria: rupture of membranes, regular uterine contractions (three or more contractions per 10 minutes), a history of prior uterine surgery (cesarean delivery or myomectomy), multiple gestations, malpresentation, contraindication to prostaglandins, nonreassuring fetal heart rate tracing (category 3 or persistent category 2), vaginal bleeding, fetal demise, anomalous fetus, or any contraindication to vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Balloon catheters plus < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
144 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sri Lanka.

Inclusion criteria: women who had singleton uncomplicated pregnancies with gestational age 40 weeks +3 days, with a vertex presentation and no contraindication for induction of labour.

Exclusion criteria: any woman with a previous caesarean delivery, history of myomectomy, hypersensitivity to misoprostol, or currently having pregnancy induced hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus or pre labour rupture of membranes, was excluded from the trial.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Single balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was conducted without external funding.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women with single live pregnancies at ≥ 37 weeks’ gestation with valid indication for induction, cephalic presentation, Bishop’s score ≤ 4, and no fetal compromise.

Exclusion criteria: absence of consent to the study, history of cesarean delivery or other uterine surgery, chorioamnionitis, and any contraindications to the use of misoprostol and /or vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus < 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. < 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
205 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Slovenia.

Inclusion criteria: age 18 years or older, singleton pregnancy, cephalic insertion of the foetus, no signs of chorioamnionitis, no previous surgery on the uterus, no contraindications for vaginal delivery, absence of uterine contractions, and unfavourable cervix (defined as a Bishop score of six points or less) at least 4 hours after PROM.

Exclusion criteria: pregnant women who met the following criteria: age less than 18 years old, previous uterine surgery (previous caesarean sections, myomectomies), multiple pregnancies, a Bishop score of seven points or higher, signs of chorioamnionitis, elevated body temperature or other signs of inflammation at the time of admission to the Department of Perinatology, an inconclusive or pathological cardiotocographic (CTG) record, and all non-cephalic pregnant women who had a positive Streptococcus B vaginal smear or urine test were given penicillin-based antibiotics on a regular basis as soon as they were admitted to the delivery room. Others were given antibiotics 8 hours after PROM, in accordance with standard hospital clinical policy.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from University Medical Center Maribor, grant number IRP-2020/01-04.

Char: Participants:
88 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Pakistan.

Inclusion criteria: women with age were between 26-40 years, multigravida, accurate dating of gestation, singleton viable pregnancy, gestational age 40-42 weeks, cephalic presentation, unfavourable cervical status defined as a Bishop score (BS) of < 6, intact membranes, patient’s height more than 150 cm.

Exclusion criteria: women with known contraindications to receiving prostaglandins, placenta previa, previous uterine surgery and any antenatal complications (medical/obstetrical).
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
300 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Israel.

Inclusion criteria: gestational age ≥ 37 weeks, parity 1–3, singleton pregnancy with a vertex presentation, unfavourable cervix (Bishop score less than 5) and intact membranes.

Exclusion criteria: previous cesarean section, lack of prenatal care, and any contraindication for vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Single balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
140 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Lithuania.

Inclusion criteria: women were eligible for enrolment if they presented with obstetric or medical indications for labour induction, prelabour rupture of membranes, chronic, gestational hypertension or mild pre-eclampsia, or gestational diabetes without the need for insulin treatment. Additional requirements for enrolment included a singleton live pregnancy at term in the cephalic presentation, absence of active labour, a normal FHR tracing and an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score ≤ 6).

Exclusion criteria: known hypersensitivity to the use of prostaglandins, previous caesarean delivery or other types of uterine surgery, chorioamnionitis or hyperthermia > 38°C, the need for immediate birth (such as ominous FHR, active uterine bleeding), ultrasonically estimated oligohydramnios, polyhydramnios, suspicion of fetal malformation, macrosomia or growth restriction and parity of more than five.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: the presence of a single live fetus in cephalic presentation and a Bishop Score of less than or equal to 6.

Exclusion criteria: women with spontaneous labour, spontaneous rupture of the membranes, a history of prior uterine surgery or any contraindication to vaginal delivery or use of prostaglandins were excluded.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
250 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Iran.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancies, live gestational age greater than or equal to 37 weeks, fetal weight less than four kilograms, amniotic fluid index greater than five, normal Bishop score less than seven, and the absence of labour pains in the mother

Exclusion criteria: rupture of membranes, restriction of fetal growth, suspicion of fetal malformation, previous uterine scar, urgent need for delivery, the number of deliveries more than five, fever above 38 degrees in the mother, or chorioamnions, estimated fetal weight of more than four kilograms, diagnosis of oligohydramnios or polyhydramnios, history of allergy to Prostaglandins and gesta0onal age were less than 37 weeks.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
206 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Canada.

Inclusion criteria: women who had indication for induction of labour, single live fetus, gestation longer than 37 completed weeks, intact membranes, and cephalic presentation.

Exclusion criteria: women who presented with any one of the following were ineligible: nonreassuring FHR tracing, previous uterine surgery, known hypersensitivity to prostaglandins, age less than 18 years, or contraindication to vaginal birth.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported in part by funding from the Health Care Corporation of St. John’s and Memorial University of Newfoundland, Faculty of Medicine, St. John’s, Newfoundland Canada.

Char: Participants:
38 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United Kingdom.

Inclusion criteria: women aged ≥ 16 years, undergoing induction of labour at ≥ 37 weeks’ gestation, with intact membranes, able to give informed consent and deemed suitable for outpatient induction of labour according to local guidelines. At both the recruiting sites, the pregnancy had to be uncomplicated at or beyond 41+0 weeks with a single foetus in cephalic presentation with no risk factors.

Exclusion criteria: out-patient induction of labour is deemed unsuitable for the following women on the grounds of safety: 1) Grand multiparous women (Parity 5 or more) Multiple pregnancy, 2) Women with complex medical or obstetric problems (i.e. placenta previa, recurrent antepartum haemorrhage, diabetes, pre-eclampsia, Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), Obstetric Cholestasis), 3) Previous caesarean section/uterine scar. 2. Women who are contracting and/ or requiring analgesia
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. Double balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from National Institute for Health Research (NIHR), research for patient benefit scheme (PB-PG-0815-20022).

Char: Participants:
140 women were randomised in a hospital setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: all the patients with leaking per vaginum at term were recruited in the trial if they fulfilled the following criteria: 1) Pregnancies between 37- 41 weeks of gestation with a singleton foetus with vertex presentation, 2) Reassuring foetal heart rate, and 3) Definite diagnosis of premature rupture of membranes.

Exclusion criteria: contraindications to vaginal delivery, Previous uterine scar, Diagnosis of labour, Clinical estimated fetal weight more than 4 kilograms, Evidence of temperature > 100.4 degree Fahrenheit, uterine tenderness or foul smelling amniotic fluid, and Any medical diseases like diabetes on insulin or severe pre-eclampsia.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in Sweden.

Inclusion criteria: (1) uncomplicated singleton pregnancy, (2) cephalic presentation, (3) gestational age at least 42 weeks, (4) Bishop score ≤ 5, (5) normal amniotic fluid index measuring > 5m, (6) reactive fetal heart pattern, and (7) intact membranes.

Exclusion criteria: regular uterine contractions, cardiorespiratory disease, history of headache, alcohol abuse, intolerance to isosorbide mononitrate, and serious disease, defined as daily use of medication.
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
108 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Canada.

Inclusion criteria: women were eligible if they presented with premature rupture of membranes diagnosed by sterile speculum examination that showed passage of fluid or arborization (or ferning) of vaginal fluid by microscopic examination and had singleton gestations greater than 37 completed weeks with cephalic presentation.

Exclusion criteria: any contraindication to vaginal birth, prior uterine surgery, active labour, active maternal bleeding, chorioamnionitis, major fetal anomalies, contraindication to prostaglandin use, and age less than 18 years.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported in part by funding from Memorial University of Newfoundland, Faculty of Medicine, St. John’s, Newfoundland, Canada, and Association of Professors of Obstetrics and Gynecology of Canada (1996 APOG/Serono Resident Research Award).

Char: Participants:
626 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom.

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous or multiparous women with a singleton pregnancy who were eligible for induction of labour with prostaglandins were included in the study. All women provided informed consent prior to participation in the study and were aged 18 years or older, had a pregnancy duration of at least 37 weeks and demonstrated an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 9).

Exclusion criteria: women who required insulin to control diabetes were excluded from the study, as were women who had a multiple pregnancy. Women in whom oxytocic drugs were contraindicated, women with a uterine scar, women with a history of prior conditions for which labour was inappropriate and women who had already ruptured their membranes were also excluded. Additional exclusion criteria were an intercurrent vaginal, ascending or systemic infection; placenta praevia, placental abruption or unexplained vaginal bleeding during the pregnancy; active cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic disease; a contraindication to vaginal delivery or a known allergy to prostaglandins.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Alliance Pharmaceuticals Limited.

Char: Participants:
160 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Turkey.

Inclusion criteria: (1) singleton live gestation with vertex presentation, (2) an indication for induction: oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index < 5 cm), preeclampsia, intrauterine growth restriction, gestational age > 41 weeks (dates confirmed by first-trimester ultra-sound), (3) Bishop score of < 5, (4) absence of spontaneous uterine contractions (i.e., less than four spontaneous contractions per hour), (5) ultrasound-estimated fetal body weight < 4,500 g, and (6) a reactive nonstress test (NST).

Exclusion criteria: known hypersensitivity to the use of prostaglandins, previous cesarean delivery or other type of uterine surgery, non-cephalic presentation, a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 before conception and previous attempt of labor induction for the present pregnancy.
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
212 women were randomised in a hospital setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: women were eligible for entry into the trial if they had ruptured membranes at ≥ 37 weeks’ gestation, had a single fetus in cephalic presentation and were not in labor. The time of spontaneous rupture of membranes was noted. Diagnosis was based on: (1) the clinical history of the passage of liquor; (2) pooling of fluid in the posterior fornix, as seen during the speculum examination; (3) palpation through the cervical canal for the absence of membranes; and (iv) reduced liquor volume on sonography (amniotic fluid index < 5) in selected women where clinical findings were inconclusive.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded from the study if they were in labor (the onset of labor was defined as regular contractions occurring twice in 10 min by abdominal palpation) or if there was a contraindication to the induction of labor (such as placenta previa or meconium staining of the amniotic fluid). Women with a history of previous caesarean delivery were also excluded.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
67 women were randomised in a hospital setting in China.

Inclusion criteria: 1) confirmed gestational age of 37-42 weeks; 2) a singleton pregnancy with a normal fetus in cephalic presentation; 3) premature rupture of membranes confirmed by visualizing a pool of amniotic fluid at a sterile speculum examination; 4) absence of other indications for urgent induction of labour; 5) rupture of membranes for < 6 h; 6) reassuring fetal heart rate tracing; 7) no signs of labour, no abdominal pain on admission.

Exclusion criteria: 1) known hypersensitivity or any contraindications to prostaglandins (e.g. glaucoma or sickle cell disease); 2) age < 18 years old; 3) group B streptococcus carrier; 4) multiple pregnancy; 5) nonreassuring cardiotocograph (CTG) or meconium-stained liquor; 6) previous uterine surgery; 7) contraindication to vaginal birth; 8) estimated fetal weight of > 4 kg or < 2 kg 9). placenta praevia or unexplained vaginal bleeding; 10) evidence of chorioamnionitis; 11) grand multipara (parity ≥ 4); 12) active medication at time of PROM or presence of any pre-existing medical disease e.g. cardiovascular disease or chronic renal failure
Char: Interventions: Placebo vs. 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
210 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Iran.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy, gestational age 37 weeks or greater, cephalic presentation, live fetus, cervical Bishop Score ≤ 5, estimated fetal weight < 4000 g, and intact membranes.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded in case of premature rupture of membranes, placenta previa, placenta abruption, fetal malformations, severe preeclampsia, and abnormal fetal heart rate tracings or signs of active labor at admission and previous uterine scars. Other exclusion criteria were the presence of contraindications for the use of PG analogs, including glaucoma, asthma, epilepsy, and allergy.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. intracervical misoprostol (but this method was not included in this review)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was conducted without external funding.

Char: Participants:
150 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: premature rupture of membranes confirmed up to 6 hours after the occurrence; gestational age ≥ 37 weeks, cephalic presentation and a live fetus showing no signs of fetal compromise as evaluated by cardiotocography.

Exclusion criteria: past caesarean section or uterine surgery; being in labour at admission as characterised by regular painful uterine contractions (two contractions in 10 minutes and gradually shortening); presence of fetal malformations incompatible with life; twin pregnancy or strongly suspected or confirmed chorioamnionitis.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Expectant management
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
202 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Switzerland.

Inclusion criteria: women admitted for induction of labour at more than 37 weeks of gestation, with a live single fetus in vertex presentation, were eligible for the study if the Bishop score was 6 or less.

Exclusion criteria: the presence of uterine scar, suspected fetal distress (nonreassuring fetal heart rate, oligohydramnios, or intrauterine growth retardation), malformation, vaginal bleeding, or contraindication for prostaglandin administration.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
198 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Spain.

Inclusion criteria: singleton uncomplicated nulliparous women with live fetus of at least 286 days of gestational age with indication for induction of labor because of post‐term pregnancy, absence of any contraindication for vaginal birth and a baseline Bishop score < 6.

Exclusion criteria: multiple pregnancies, multiparity, stillbirth, oligohydramnios, suspected fetal distress, severe asthma, any known allergy or intolerance to prostaglandin agents or any contraindication for vaginal delivery. A verbal and written informed consent was obtained from all individual participants included in the study.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
123 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: gestational age and ≥ 37 weeks, Bishop index < 8, single, live fetus and indication for termination of pregnancy.

Exclusion criteria: fetal weight estimated by ultrasound equal to or greater than 4,000 g, anomalous presentations, severe oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index less than 5), fetus not reactive to cardiotocography or sound stimulation, fetal malformations, fever (temperature ≥ 38 oC), uterine scarring and other possible contraindications for vaginal delivery (placenta previa, placental abruption, genital herpes, HIV seropositive).
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: two forms of misoprostol used in this study were supplied by the Hebron laboratory.

Char: Participants:
80 women were randomised in a hospital setting in France.

Inclusion criteria: women with a live, singleton gestation at term (37 or more weeks of gestation) with PROM (clinical amniotic fluid leakage and/or positive insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 (IGFBP1) test), an unfavourable cervical examination (Bishop score < 6), and no contraindication to labour.

Exclusion criteria: maternal exclusion criteria included those in active labour, suspected intraamniotic infection, detection of group B Streptococcus on any vaginal or urinary sample during the current or any previous pregnancy, placental abruption or significant haemorrhage, any prior uterine surgery including caesarean delivery, any contraindication to vaginal delivery, human immunodeficiency virus, or herpetic genital lesions. Fetal exclusion criteria were non-cephalic presentation, severe fetal anomalies, intrauterine fetal demise, growth restriction < 3rd percentile with Doppler anomalies, and non-reassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) tracing.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus oxytocin vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was conducted without external funding.

Char: Participants:
1220 women were randomised in a hospital setting in France.

Inclusion criteria: women were eligible for the study if they were 18 years old or more, had a singleton pregnancy, a fetus in vertex presentation with a term between 41 weeks + 0 days and 42 weeks + 0 (estimated from an ultrasound between 11 and 14 weeks), and had agreed with their obstetric professional that their labour should be induced.

Exclusion criteria: a Bishop score ≥ 6, severe pre-eclampsia, a previous cesarean delivery or other uterine surgery, low-lying placenta, suspected genital herpes infection, known HIV seropositivity, suspected severe congenital abnormalities, pathological FHR, or prelabour rupture of membranes (PROM).
Char: Interventions: Double balloon catheter vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the French Ministry of Health (Programme Hospitalier de Recherche Clinique 2015, PHRCN-2015).

Char: Participants:
741 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Australia.

Inclusion criteria: women with a singleton pregnancy at ≥ 36+6 weeks’ gestation.

Exclusion criteria: women with a favourable cervix (defined as a modified Bishop score of ≥ 7), any contraindication to vaginal birth, previous uterine surgery (including caesarean section), or ruptured membranes.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists and Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide.

Char: Participants:
50 women were randomised in a hospital setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: women with heart disease who were registered in the cardio-obstetric clinic were recruited consecutively between 38-41 weeks’ gestation after obtaining informed consent. Women with a known case of heart disease with New York Heart Association class I-II and cephalic singleton gestation were included in the study.

Exclusion criteria: women with previous cesarean section, primary pulmonary hypertension, Eisenmenger syndrome, Marfan syndrome, left heart obstruction, prior cardiac event or arrhythmia, malformed fetus, severe anaemia (< 7 g/dL), intrauterine fetal death, other obstetric indications for induction of labour, and patients on anticoagulation were excluded from the study.
Char: Interventions: Oxytocin (alone) vs. Expectant management
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
100 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom.

Inclusion criteria: (1) singleton pregnancy; (2) cephalic presentation; (3) gestation of more than 37 weeks (confirmed by ultrasound); (4) Bishop’s score ≤ 7, and (5) a normal admission cardiotocograph.

Exclusion criteria: women with proteinuric hypertension were excluded.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
150 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy, gestational age of 37 weeks or greater, live fetus, cephalic presentation, estimated sonographic fetal weight less than 4000 g, amniotic fluid index greater than 5 cm, normal antepartum non-stress test results, and Bishop score of 6 or less.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded in cases of fetal malformations, intrauterine growth restriction, previous uterine scars, premature rupture of membranes, or any contraindication to vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: Misoprostol tablets used in this study were donated by the Hebron S/A Ind. Quimicas e Farmacêuticas, Caruaru, Brazil.

Char: Participants:
80 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Venezuela.

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton pregnancies at term, with cephalic vertex presentation, who were not in labour (less than 2 centimeters dilated, less than 60% dilated, and less than 3 painful uterine contractions per hour) and without history of previous uterine interventions.

Exclusion criteria: women with a Bishop score greater than 5, rupture of membranes, chorioamnionitis, vaginal bleeding, twin pregnancies, presentations other than vertex cephalic, diagnosis of placenta previa or placental abruption, alterations in uterine contractility, liver alterations, renal or cardiovascular, with contraindications for the use of oxytocin or a history of hypersensitivity to latex or who refused to participate in the research.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus oxytocin vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: indication for induction of labour, gestational age ≥ 37 weeks, single live fetus, vertex presentation, Bishop score ≤ 6, estimated fetal weight < 4000 g, amniotic fluid index > 5 and good fetal well-being.

Exclusion criteria: previous caesarean section, previous uterine scar resulting from uterine surgery, genital bleeding of unknown origin, fetal abnormalities, chorioamnionitis, tumours, malformations and/or ulceration in the vulvar or perineal region or birth canal that could be harmful to mother or child during the expulsion stage of labour, and HIV positivity.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes:
2 women (< 10%) were excluded from the analyses because they refused to participate in the trial after randomisation. Numbers were similar across both arms. All other women were included in the analysis.

Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
307 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 years or older presenting for induction of labor at 37 weeks of gestation or more with an established plan for preinduction cervical ripening were screened for eligibility. Women with an unfavourable cervix, defined as having Bishop scores less than 6, with no contraindication for vaginal delivery were eligible for the trial.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded if there was fetal death, prior uterine scar, major fetal congenital anomaly, nonreassuring fetal heart rate tracing, premature rupture of membranes, severe pre-eclampsia, chorioamnionitis, or active vaginal bleeding.
Char: Interventions: Osmotic cervical dilators vs. < 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Medicem Technology s.r.o., Czech Republic.

Char: Participants:
72 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Iran.

Inclusion criteria: primiparous women with uncomplicated pregnancies and a gestational age of over 40 weeks. Participants were selected based on an ultrasound conducted before 20 weeks, confirming a singleton pregnancy with cephalic fetal presentation. Other requirements included a Bishop score between 4 and 5, an adequate amniotic fluid index (AFI), a regular fetal heart rate, and healthy membranes.

Exclusion criteria: women with regular uterine contractions, at least 45-second contractions in 10 minutes, history of headache, intolerance to isorbide mononitrate, serious cardio-pulmonary disease, pregnancy with placental abruption, umbilical cord prolapse, history of caesarean section or previous myomectomy, pelvic stenosis, cervical cancer based on pathology, irregular fetal heart rate pattern, tachycardia, bradycardia deceleration) multiple pregnancy, non-cephalic presentation of polyhydramnios, severe high blood pressure of the mother 110/160 and proteinuria +1), baby's weight over 3500 grams based on estimated fetal weight or ultrasound, hydrocephalus, and the small size of the mother.
Char: Interventions: Placebo vs. Nitric oxide donors
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
152 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sri Lanka.

Inclusion criteria: women with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies having a cephalic presentation and a cervix unfavourable for induction of labour (Bishop score < 6) at a period of gestation of 40 weeks and 6 days.

Exclusion criteria: women with multiple pregnancies, malpresentation, pregnancies with previous caesarean section or any contraindication for normal delivery or for the use of misoprostol, or had received any prior intervention for ripening of the cervix.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. < 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: misoprostol tablets used in this study were supplied by Dr. Kurian Joseph, Joseph’s Nursing Home, Chennai, India.

Char: Participants:
420 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Singapore and Malaysia.

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women aged from 21 to 40 years old, with a singleton pregnancy and no major foetal anomaly who were suitable for vaginal delivery and scheduled for a planned inducton of labour from 37+0 to 41+6 weeks gestation were included into the study.

Exclusion criteria: women with spontaneous labour at start of planned induction, bishop score more than 6 and cervical dilation more than or equal to 3 cm at the start of induction or with confirmed rupture of membranes were excluded. Women with abnormal cardiotocograph at the start of induction, with any indication for caesarean delivery or a previous scarred uterus were also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Double balloon catheter vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from SingHealth DukeNUS OBGYN Academic Clinical Program (ACP) Grant.

Char: Participants:
444 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom.

Inclusion criteria: primigravidae admitted at term with prelabour rupture of the membranes.

Exclusion criteria: multigravidae; Gestational age ≤ 36 weeks; Speculum examination revealed no amniotic fluid in the vagina Contractions occurring once in 10 min or more often Meconium-stained amniotic fluid; Multiple pregnancy; Breech presentation; Abnormal fetal heart rate trace on admission Pre-eclampsia; Known or suspected intrauterine growth retardation Diabetes mellitus; Any other significant medical disorder of pregnancy.
Char: Interventions: Expectant management vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
674 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom.

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women scheduled for induction of labour who were ≥ 16 years of age, capable of providing informed consent, with a singleton pregnancy at ≥ 37+0 weeks’ gestation (determined by ultrasound dating scan), and with the fetus in a vertex presentation with intact membranes were eligible for inclusion.

Exclusion criteria: women already receiving oxytocin, those who had a diagnosis of fulminant preeclampsia or eclampsia, and those who had a contraindication to Dilapan-S or dinoprostone were ineligible.
Char: Interventions: Osmotic cervical dilators vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Medicem Technology s.r.o., Czech Republic with an unrestricted research grant.

Char: Participants:
319 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: women who presented to the labor and delivery unit for delivery who required cervical ripening were eligible for the trial. Women ≥ 14 years of age undergoing either a medically indicated induction of labour at a gestational age beyond 37 0/7 weeks or an elective induction of labour after 39 weeks with a singleton pregnancy in the cephalic presentation, and a modified Bishop score 6 (commonly used as a cutoff for the need for cervical ripening), were eligible for enrollment.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded if they had a known prior uterine scar, untreated cervical infection, known major fetal congenital anomaly, or evidence of fetal compromise (category 2 or 3 fetal tracings) before the start of the induction.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: this work was supported solely by internal Department funds for resident research.

Char: Participants:
102 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in Egypt.

Inclusion criteria: the participants were pregnant women who required labor induction for unfavorable cervices (Bishop Score less than 6) and who were in a condition appropriate for outpatient cervical ripening for 36 hours. Each had a singleton pregnancy with a live fetus at least 37 weeks of gestation, absence of uterine contractions, and intact membranes.

Exclusion criteria: fetal malpresentation, placenta previa, previous uterine incisions, or any contraindication of labour induction listed in the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists educational bulletin on labour induction
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
5,041 women were randomised in a hospital and community setting in Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, Israel, Sweden, and Denmark.

Inclusion criteria: women who had ruptured membranes, were at ≥ 37 weeks’ gestation, and had a single fetus in a cephalic presentation.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded from the study if they were in active labour, if there had been a previous, failed attempt to induce labour, or if there was a contraindication to either induction of labour (such as placenta previa) or expectant management (such as meconium staining of the amniotic fluid or chorioamnionitis).
Char: Interventions: Oxytocin (alone) vs. Expectant management (oxytocin) vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Expectant management (vaginal dinoprostone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the Medical Research Council of Canada (Grant No. MA-11392).

Char: Participants:
101 women were randomised in a hospital and community setting in Australia.

Inclusion criteria: women ≥ 18 years old with a gestational age of 37 weeks or more, requiring induction of labour with a cervical preparation procedure (Bishop Score < 7 and cervical dilation < 2 cm).

Exclusion criteria: 1) unsuitable for outpatient management, 2) unsuitable for randomisation to either prostaglandin E2 (e.g. previous caesarean section) or catheter use (e.g. latex allergy), or prior attempted induction of labour in this pregnancy, 3) no longer requiring cervical preparation (Bishop score ≥ 7 or cervical dilatation ≥ 2 cm), had ruptured membranes, or evidence of regular uterine contractions at time of booked induction, 4) multiple pregnancy or non-vertex presentation, 5) unable to give informed consent (e.g. secondary to insufficient English), or 6) consent was declined
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
107 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Switzerland.

Inclusion criteria: women at term (between 37 and 42 completed weeks of pregnancy), with singleton fetuses in vertex presentation and less than three spontaneous uterine contractions per 30 minutes.

Exclusion criteria: previous uterine surgery, placenta previa, fetal anomaly, known allergy against prostaglandins, maternal age < 18 years and pathologic non-stress cardiotocogram prior to induction.
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the scientific pool of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, University of Basel, Switzerland.

Char: Participants:
120 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: (1) singleton gestation, (2) intact membranes, (3) Bishop score ≤ 4, (4) uterine contractions < 8 per hour, (5) cephalic presentation, (6) estimated gestational age of at least 381/2 weeks by either first or second-trimester ultrasound, (7) normal amniotic fluid index measuring > 5 cm and a reactive fetal heart rate pattern, and (8) good compliance with clinic appointments and home blood glucose monitoring.

Exclusion criteria: women who demonstrated any of the following were excluded from participation in the study: (1) multifetal gestation, (2) estimated fetal weight > 4500 g or < 2000 g, (3) prior uterine surgery, (4) rupture of membranes, (5) placenta previa or unexplained vaginal bleeding, (6) active genital herpes, glaucoma or elevated intraocular pressure, (7) hypersensitivity to prostaglandins (PGs) (8) significant renal, hepatic, or cardiovascular disease, (9) evidence of preeclampsia, (10) severe asthma, or (11) parity ≥ 6.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
114 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Japan.

Inclusion criteria: (1) pregnant women at term ≥ 41 weeks 0 day and ≤ 41 weeks 6 days at the baseline visit; (2) women aged ≥ 20 at the screening visit; (3) candidates for pharmacological labour induction; (4) patients with insufficient cervical ripening, defined as baseline Bishop score ≤ 4 at baseline visit; (5) women with a singleton pregnancy with live fetus in the vertex presentation; and (6) patients with parity ≤ 3 (parity is defined as one or more live births or stillbirths after 22 weeks 0 day of gestation).

Exclusion criteria: (1) women in labour; (2) women with uterine or cervical scars, including scars from previous cesarean section and previous cone biopsy of the cervix and loop electrosurgical excision procedure; (3) women with uterine abnormality (e.g. bicornate uterus); and (4) women administered oxytocin, any cervical ripening or labour-inducing agents (including mechanical methods) or a tocolytic drug within 7 days prior to Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP) administration.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Ferring Pharmaceutical.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Iran.

Inclusion criteria: first singleton pregnancy, minimum gestational age of 37 weeks, cephalic presentation, having a live fetus, estimated fetal weight < 4000 grams, and the Bishop score < 7.

Exclusion criteria: hypersensitivity to prostaglandins, previous uterine scar, fetal congenital malformations, intrauterine growth restriction, non-reassuring fetal heart rate, gestational age < 37 weeks, oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index < 5 cm), placenta previa, abnormal fetal presentation, and minimum Bishop score = 8. Additionally, women with diabetes, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, or epilepsy were all excluded from the study.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Shiraz University of Medical Sciences (Grant No. 90-5589).

Char: Participants:
824 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the Netherlands.

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women scheduled for induction of labour beyond 37 weeks of gestation with a vital singleton pregnancy in cephalic presentation, intact membranes, and an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 6).

Exclusion criteria: women younger than 18 years, with a previous caesarean section, placenta praevia, lethal fetal congenital anomaly, or known hypersensitivity for one of the products used for induction.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
232 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the Netherlands.

Inclusion criteria: women over 18 years of age with term pregnancy, requiring induction of labour at term with an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 6).

Exclusion criteria: prior caesarean delivery, non-vertex presentation of the fetus, ruptured membranes, hypersensitivity to one of the products used for induction, or a lethal congenital anomaly of the fetus.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
414 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Jordan.

Inclusion criteria: women aged 15 years or more, pregnancy at term with singleton live fetus in vertex presentation, intact membranes and Bishop score < 6.

Exclusion criteria: previous caesarean section or history of other uterine surgery, history of antepartum haemorrhage, non-vertex presentation, twin pregnancy, cephalo pelvic disproportion, acute fetal distress revealed by a non-stress test prior to induction, signs of infection, ruptured membranes, estimated fetal weight > 4300, or known allergy to Prostaglandin.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Single balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
118 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: (1) obstetric or medical indication for labour induction; (2) singleton gestation; (3) gestational age of ≥ 37 completed weeks by reliable dating criteria (a first- or second-trimester uterine examination and sonogram confirming the gestational age); (4) vertex presentation; (5) intact amniotic membranes; (6) bishop score of ≤ 4; and (7) reassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) pattern.

Exclusion criteria: (1) unexplained third-trimester vaginal bleeding or placenta previa; (2) non-reassuring FHR patterns; (3) active herpes simplex virus infection; (4) history of asthma or glaucoma; (5) a strong clinical suspicion of fetopelvic disproportion; (6) parity of ≥ 6; (7) ruptured membranes; (8) previous caesarean delivery or any type of uterine scar; and (9) macrosomia defined as an estimated fetal weight of > 4000 g for diabetic patients and > 4500 g for non-diabetic patients.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol (we did not include this group in the review)
Char: Notes: Funding source: study drugs used in this study and randomisation process were supplied by Rondell Jaggers, Pharm D. and Grace Williams, Pharm D.

Char: Participants:
142 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Tanzania.

Inclusion criteria: singleton vertex presentation; gestational age > 36 weeks.

Exclusion criteria: previous myomectomy, uteroplasty, or caesarean section.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in South Korea.

Inclusion criteria: (1) pregnancy of 37 weeks or longer, which is an indication for induction, (2) singleton pregnancy, (3) parietal position pregnancy, (4) Bishop score of 5 or less, (5) normal fetal heartbeat, and (6) cases in which the amniotic membrane was not ruptured.

Exclusion criteria: (1) vaginal bleeding of unknown cause, (2) glaucoma, hypertension, etc., where prostaglandin use is contraindicated, (3) history of caesarean section, (4) membrane rupture, and (5) decline to participate in the trial.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
129 women were randomised in a hospital and community setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: low-risk parous women were offered elective induction of labour and included if they were at least 18 years old with a singleton fetus in vertex presentation and their estimated gestational age was between 39 0/7 and 42 0/7 weeks of gestation. Furthermore, women had to have reliable transportation, access to a telephone, and reside within 30 minutes of our hospital. Lastly, cervical examination immediately before enrollment had to be 3 cm or less dilation.

Exclusion criteria: fetal growth restriction (defined as estimated fetal weight less than the 10th percentile), oligohydramnios, polyhydramnios, prior caesarean delivery or uterine surgery involving the myometrium, chronic hypertension requiring more than one antihypertensive medication, diabetes mellitus other than White’s class A1, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, hepatitis B or C infection, human immunodeficiency virus infection, fetal anomalies or demise, nonreassuring antenatal testing (defined as minimal or absent variability, abnormal baseline, or presence of decelerations), evidence of labour, and other serious medical conditions deemed by the attending physician to preclude outpatient cervical ripening. Non-English-speaking women were excluded because of our inability to provide 24-hour immediate telephone support in languages other than English.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. Balloon catheters plus oxytocin
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
160 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Canada.

Inclusion criteria: all women requiring induction of labour at or beyond term (37-42 weeks of gestation).

Exclusion criteria: previous uterine scar, oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index < 2.5th centile), intrauterine growth restriction (estimated fetal weight < 10th centile), prelabour rupture of membranes, multifetal pregnancy, and cervix favourable for amniotomy.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
62 women were randomised in a hospital setting in France.

Inclusion criteria: gestational age > 37 weeks, single fetus in cephalic presentation, normal fetal reactivity, Bishop score ≤ 5, age 18 years and over.

Exclusion criteria: ruptured membranes, major fetal anomalies, placenta previa or bottom inserted, third-trimester haemorrhage, positive HIV, hepatitis B or C serology, active genital herpes lesions, hypersensitivity to prostaglandins, contraindication to vaginal delivery, inability to provide informed consent, parity > 6, Fetal death, anterior uterine incision, chorioamnionitis, glaucoma, epilepsy, heart or vascular disease, renal or liver failure, and severe polyhydramnios.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
491 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: participants were at least 18 years of age with a full-term (37 weeks of gestation or greater), singleton gestation in cephalic presentation. Both nulliparous and multiparous women were included. Women were required to have intact membranes, a Bishop score of 6 or less, and cervical dilation of 2 cm or less.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded if there was a contraindication to a vaginal delivery or to misoprostol, fetal demise, or major fetal anomaly. Non–English-speaking women, women with human immunodeficiency virus, and women with medical conditions requiring an assisted second stage were also excluded. Additional exclusion criteria were as follows: category 3 fetal heart rate tracing; hemolysis elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count syndrome or eclampsia; growth restriction less than the 10th percentile (based on Hadlock growth curves) with reversal of flow in umbilical artery Doppler studies; and growth restriction less than the fifth percentile with elevated, absent, or reversal of flow in umbilical artery Doppler studies.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Balloon catheters plus < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Single balloon catheter vs. Balloon catheters plus oxytocin
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported in part by a career development award in Women’s Reproductive Health (Research: K12-HD001265-15) and the Maternal and Child Health Research fund from the University of Pennsylvania.

Char: Participants:
130 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Israel.

Inclusion criteria: gestational age ≥ 37 weeks, singletons in cephalic presentation, premature rupture of membranes ≤ 4 hours without contractions and a Bishop score ≤ 5.

Exclusion criteria: parity of three or more, prior uterine scar, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, maternal temperature > 37.5 C, or the presence of a non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing. The interval of ≤ 4 hours was chosen in order to avoid a potential early versus late treatment bias.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
50 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Hong Kong.

Inclusion criteria: women admitted with an obstetric or medical indication for labour induction and fulfilling the following criteria were included: (1) gestation of ≥ 37 weeks ascertained by dating scan before 20 weeks of gestation, (2) nulliparity, (3) having a live single conceptus in a cephalic presentation, (4) Bishop score > 5, and (5) normal 30-minute foetal heart tracing. Only nulliparous women were included to eliminate the confounding effect of parity and enhance patient safety.

Exclusion criteria: women with the following conditions were excluded: (1) known hypersensitivity or any contraindication to prostaglandins (eg glaucoma), (2) previous uterine scar, and (3) any confirmed or suspected membrane rupture.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. Oxytocin plus amniotomy
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
100 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom.

Inclusion criteria: women with spontaneous rupture of the membrane and singleton uncomplicated pregnancies, cephalic presentation, and no uterine activity.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded from the study if they had any of the following conditions: previous serious antepartum haemorrhage, fetal growth retardation, diabetes mellitus, Rh immunization, moderate preeclampsia, history of venereal disease, previous caesarean delivery, temperature above 37.5 oC on admission, ruptured membranes for longer than 12 hours, or meconium-stained amniotic fluid (AF) on admission.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Expectant management
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
177 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous, primiparous and multiparous who controlled their date of last menstruation, and who had a term progressive pregnancy, mono-fetal, with fetal heart rate in the standards (110-160 beats per minute), cephalic presentation, without medical or obstetric indication of labour induction and having signed the informed consent.

Exclusion criteria: pregnant women who had already delivered more than five times, twin pregnancy, hypertensive disorders, diabetes, presentation other than cephalic, FHR anomaly before onset, large pregnant uterus, placenta previa, scarred or fibromyomatous uterus, anomalies of the maternal pelvis and cases of fetal death.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
68 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: women older than 18 years who had completed at least 40 weeks of pregnancy, with a Bishop score of less than 9, and a well-dated pregnancy were eligible for inclusion.

Exclusion criteria: any current obstetric indication for induction of labour, including oligohydramnios defined as an amniotic fluid index of less than 5.0 cm, ruptured membranes, the presence of any contraindication to a trial of labour including fetal malpresentation or vaginal bleeding, multiple gestation, regular uterine contractions defined as 10 or more per hour, and a history of a prior caesarean delivery.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
240 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 6) and normal fetal heart rate.

Exclusion criteria: multiple gestations, non-cephalic presentation, previous caesarean delivery or uterine scar, rupture of membranes, antepartum bleeding, genital herpes infection, fetal death, placenta previa or previous attempts to induce labour.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Balloon catheters plus oxytocin
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from CAPES (an institution of the Brazilian Government for the improvement of human resources in university)

Char: Participants:
602 women were randomised in a hospital setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: we included women who were at least 18 years of age, at 20 weeks’ gestation or later with a live fetus, and in whom the decision had been made to induce vaginal birth because of pre-eclampsia or hypertension.

Exclusion criteria: we excluded women who were unable to give informed consent, those with a history of caesarean section, multiple pregnancy, ruptured membranes, clinically diagnosed chorioamnionitis, or a history of allergy to misoprostol.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. < 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes:
The authors of this study made their raw data available to the public. We only kept data of women at or beyond 37 weeks of gestational age. After applying this criterion, we discovered that the dataset only contained information about women who had not undergone a previous caesarean section. Finally, we used the data from 475 women.

Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Medical Research Council, Department for International Development, and Wellcome Trust Joint Global Health Trials Scheme.

Char: Participants:
170 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Lebanon.

Inclusion criteria: women with live singletons in cephalic presentation at ≥ 37 weeks of gestation admitted with a medical or obstetric indication for labour induction and with a Bishop score of < 8.

Exclusion criteria: active labour, previous caesarean section or uterine scar, known contraindications to prostaglandin use (e.g. asthma), grand multiparity (five or more), fetal congenital malformations, nonreassuring fetal heart tracing (NRFH), and significant fetal or maternal concerns (e.g. intrauterine growth restriction, severe preeclampsia). Active labour was defined as cervical dilation of ≥ 3 cm and regular contractions. NRFH was defined as late or severe variable decelerations, tachycardia, or loss of beat-to-beat variability.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the University Research Board (URB) at the American University of Beirut.

Char: Participants:
106 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Thailand.

Inclusion criteria: all women requiring elective induction of labour at or beyond term (37–42 completed weeks of gestation with ultrasound confirmed date), which coordinated with the study were assessed for entry into the study. Inclusion criteria included singleton pregnancy with parity of not more than 4, vertex presentation, normal fetal heart rate tracing, initial Bishop score ≤ 4, no premature contraction, and no premature rupture of membranes.

Exclusion criteria: women with previous uterine surgery including a previous caesarean section, with significant fetal or medical concern or known contraindications to the use of prostaglandins were excluded.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
135 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Nigeria.

Inclusion criteria: parturients who gave consent, had low bishop score (≤ 5), term singleton cephalic presenting fetus with intact membranes and no contraindication to vaginal delivery were recruited into the study.

Exclusion criteria: women who refused consent, preterm delivery, vaginal infection, non-cephalic presentation, multiple gestation, low-lying placenta/previa, vaginal bleeding, previous caesarean section and ruptured membranes.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
100 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: a gestational age between 38.0 and 40.0 weeks, a cervical Bishop score ≤ 6, absence of a medical indication for delivery, and no more than one previous low-transverse caesarean delivery

Exclusion criteria: women with a nonreactive nonstress test, oligohydramnios (defined as an amniotic fluid index < 5.0 cm), macrosomia (defined as an estimated fetal weight > 4000 gm), or growth restriction (defined as an estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile).
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
78 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in Nigeria.

Inclusion criteria: women were considered eligible for this study if they had a singleton gestation in cephalic presentation and a Bishop score of ≤ 8 at 40 weeks gestation, and a lack of current indication for induction of labour.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded from the study if they had rupture of membranes, unexplained vaginal bleeding, a prior uterine incision, a non-reactive non-stress test and an estimated fetal weight of > 4500g. Women were excluded if the non-stress test was non-reactive or non-reassuring, if rupture of membranes was present, or if the Bishop score was more than 8.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. No treatment
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
160 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: indication for induction of labour who formally consented to participate in the study, gestational age from 37 weeks, single fetus, live, cephalic and Bishop score ≤ 4.

Exclusion criteria: the presence of uterine scarring, rupture of membranes, estimated fetal weight greater than 4000 g, placenta previa, clinical or laboratory condition compatible with chorioamnionitis, information on allergy to prostaglandins and maternal and/or fetal conditions were considered. that required the immediate termination of pregnancy.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
400 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United Kingdom

Inclusion criteria: nulliparity, singleton fetus, cephalic presentation, > 38 completed weeks of gestation, modified Bishop score < 6, normal admission cardiotocograph, and ability to comprehend the nature of the study.

Exclusion criteria: women with any of the contraindications listed in the British National Formulary to prostaglandin E2 (active cardiac, pulmonary, renal, or hepatic disease; placenta praevia or unexplained vaginal bleeding during pregnancy and ruptured membranes; major cephalopelvic disproportion or fetal malpresentation; history of caesarean delivery or major uterine surgery; untreated pelvic infection; and fetal distress) or isosorbide mononitrate (hypersensitivity to nitrates, hypotensive conditions and hypovolemia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, aortic or mitral stenosis, cardiac tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, marked anaemia, and closed-angle glaucoma). Other exclusion criteria were delivery mandatory within the next 48 hours in the maternal or fetal interest, ≥ 1 births at > 23 weeks of gestation, age < 16 years, or ruptured fetal membranes.
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the Sir Jules Thorn Charitable Trust (reference no. 01/02 A).

Char: Participants:
112 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Turkey.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy ≥ 37 weeks of gestation (37–42 weeks), a maternal–fetal indication of labour induction, cephalic presentation, intact amniochorionic membranes, a cervical Bishop score of < 4, reassuring fetal heart rate.

Exclusion criteria: fetal congenital abnormalities, parity > 5, any contraindication for vaginal delivery, antepartum bleeding of unknown etiology, cardiopulmonary, renal, hepatic disease, glaucoma, known hypersensitivity to prostaglandins, cephalopelvic disproportion, estimated fetal birth weight over 4,500 g in nondiabetic and over 4,000 g in diabetic patients, placenta previa, known or suspected chorioamnionitis, previous uterine scar (myomectomy or caesarean delivery).
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
146 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Thailand.

Inclusion criteria: (1) singleton gestation in a cephalic presentation, (2) reassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) pattern, (3) unfavourable cervix (was defined as Bishop score of < 6), (4) gestational age > 41 weeks without labour pain or > 37 weeks with indications for labour induction such as hypertension, oligohydramnios, intrauterine growth restriction, and gestational diabetes mellitus, (5) intact amniotic membranes, and (6) absence of uterine contraction observed in a 20-minute interval.

Exclusion criteria: (1) estimated fetal weight of > 4,000 g or evidence of cephalopelvic disproportion, (2) parity of > 6, (3) previous caesarean delivery or history of uterine incision, (4) any contraindication to vaginal delivery such as placenta previa, vasa previa and active genital herpes simplex infection, (5) evidence of chorioamnionitis as determined by maternal temperature > 100.4 F and the presence of either uterine tenderness or, foul-smelling amniotic fluid, or both, and (6) any contraindication for prostaglandin use eg. history of glaucoma or preexisting cardiac disease.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
670 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom.

The entry criteria for the study were: women over the age of 16 years with singleton pregnancy at 37– 42 weeks of gestation, live fetus in cephalic presentation, intact membranes, no history of antepartum haemorrhage, no previous caesarean section or history of uterine surgery and no allergy or severe asthma in response to prostaglandins.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the Fetal Medicine Foundation (Registered Charity 1037116).

Char: Participants:
163 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Greece.

Inclusion criteria: 1) age > 18 years old, 2) nulliparity, 3) accurate dating of gestation, including crown rump length (CRL) measurements in the first trimester of pregnancy, 4) singleton viable pregnancy, 5) gestational age ≥ 285 days, 6) cephalic presentation, 7) unfavourable cervical status defined as a Bishop score (BS) of ≤ 5, 8) intact membranes, and 9) reactive non-stress test (NST).

Exclusion criteria: 1) known contraindications to receiving prostaglandins, 2) placenta previa, 3) prior uterine surgery, and 4) any antenatal complications.
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
126 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: low risk primigravid and multigravid women with a singleton fetus in cephalic presentation at gestational age between 38+4 and 40 weeks with Bishop’s score < 4 with no indication for immediate induction.

Exclusion criteria: women with ruptured membranes, unexplained vaginal bleeding, prior uterine surgery, clinically estimated fetal weight more than 4 kg and associated obstetric complications like gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, fetal growth restriction, etc.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
592 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sweden.

Inclusion criteria: completion of a full-term pregnancy together with one or more of the common indications for induction of labour, including postterm pregnancy, premature rupture of membranes, pre-eclampsia, oligohydramnios, diabetes and psychosocial parameters. In addition, an absence of spontaneous contractions and a Bishop score of ≤ 6 were also required.

Exclusion criteria: contraindications for the administration of prostaglandins and/or for vaginal delivery, a previous caesarean section or other form of uterine surgery, breech presentation, signs of infection and/or the necessity for immediate delivery as indicated by, for example, pathological cardiotocography at the time of admission.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Single balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
228 women were randomised in a hospital setting in India.

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous or multiparous with a singleton pregnancy between 37 and 42 weeks’ gestation, with obstetric or medical indications for induction of labour and an unfavourable cervix (initial Bishop score of ≤ 6), a vertex presentation, a reactive fetal heart rate pattern, and absence of uterine contractions.

Exclusion criteria: women were excluded from the study if they had a malpresentation, uterine contractions, suspected cephalo–pelvic disproportion, an estimated fetal weight > 4000 g (by clinical assessment and ultrasonography), maternal age < 18 years, parity of ≥ 5, a favourable cervix (Bishop score > 6), a previous Caesarean section or uterine scar, multiple gestations, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, fetal distress, suspected chorioamnionitis, or a contraindication to vaginal delivery or to administration of prostaglandins.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
156 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sri Lanka.

Inclusion criteria: women with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies and cephalic presentations of the fetus at 41 weeks’ gestation, where the dates had been confirmed by an early ultrasound scan, and having an unfavorable cervix with a modified Bishop Score of less than five, were recruited for the study.

Exclusion criteria: women with any medical or obstetric problems and any contraindications for the use of isosorbide mononitrate-sustained release were excluded.
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
118 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancies scheduled for induction of labour for postdate (42 week) reasons alone and with an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score < 5) were considered for entry into the study.

Exclusion criteria: women who had regular uterine contractions and had undergone amniocentesis before enrollment.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
215 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: women at 18 years or older, had Bishop scores of 4 or less, carried singleton pregnancies in cephalic presentation, and had reached a gestational age of at least 37 weeks.

Exclusion criteria: a uterine scar, vaginal bleeding, ruptured membranes, history of adult asthma or glaucoma, grand multiparity (four or more previous births), and evidence of nonreassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) test results (persistent nonreactive nonstress test or positive contraction stress test).
Char: Interventions: Placebo vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Controlled Therapeutics, Malvern, Pennsylvania.

Char: Participants:
140 women were randomised in a hospital setting in France. 

Inclusion criteria: all patients were offered participation in this randomized clinical trial whenever prostaglandin induction was indicated for postterm pregnancy or intrauterine growth restriction. The inclusion criteria were singleton pregnancy, cephalic presentation, Bishop score ≤ 5, and < 4 spontaneous uterine contractions per hour.

Exclusion criteria: < 18 years old or when a nonstress test suggested acute fetal distress before induction. Fetal-pelvic disproportion, placenta previa, preterm rupture of membranes, breech or transverse lie, previous caesarean delivery, and known allergy to prostaglandins also were considered as noninclusion criteria.
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
419 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women who were at 37 weeks 0 days or greater of gestation with a favourable cervix (≤ 3 cm dilated and ≤ 60% effaced) and a live singleton fetus in cephalic presentation, who had no contraindication to vaginal delivery, and who had a scheduled induction of labour were screened for eligibility.

Exclusion criteria: women with ruptured membranes, favourable cervix, estimated fetal weight > 5000 g for nondiabetic or > 4500 g for diabetic, chorioamnionitis, prior uterine scar, active vaginal bleeding, or nonreassuring fetal status requiring immediate delivery were excluded.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. Osmotic cervical dilators
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Medicem.

Char: Participants:
205 women were randomised in a hospital setting in France.

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women at a term exceeding 37 weeks, who had a medical indication for induction of labour, a single previous caesarean delivery with a lower segment caesarean section, a singleton pregnancy in vertex presentation, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score ≤ 4) and no premature rupture of membranes (PROM).

Exclusion criteria: younger than 18 years old or if they met one of the following exclusion criteria: placenta previa, PROM, uterine scar other than lower segment caesarean section, cervical infection (except carriage of Streptococcus agalactiae), multiple pregnancy, breech or transverse presentation, indication for a repeat caesarean or a latex allergy.
Char: Interventions: Foley single balloon catheter vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from "Programme Hospitalier de Recherche Clinique Interrégional 2010" of the French Ministry of Health (A00409‐30).

Char: Participants:
50 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United States.

Inclusion criteria: women with a gestational age of 287 days (based on last menstrual period and confirmed by early clinical examination and/or early sonogram) and a cervix unfavorable for induction (Bishop score below 9) were considered candidates for this study.

Exclusion criteria: women with diabetes, hypertension, previous uterine surgery, abnormal fetal heart rate (FHR) tracings, vaginal bleeding, spontaneous rupture of membranes, or established regular uterine contractions, or sonographic evidence of nonvertex presentation, macrosomia (fetal weight estimated to be more than 4500 g), fetal anomalies, fetal growth retardation, oligohydramnios, or multiple gestation.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
80 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in the United States

Inclusion criteria: women with uncomplicated pregnancies, gestational age of at least 41 weeks by reliable dating criteria, and cervical Bishop score less than 9 were enrolled after consent was obtained.

Exclusion criteria: women complicated by maternal medical problems, previous uterine surgery, previous stillbirth, abnormal fetal heart rate (FHR), vaginal bleeding, spontaneous rupture of membranes, regular uterine contractions, abnormal ultrasound findings, or estimated fetal weight of 4500 g or higher were excluded.
Char: Interventions: Placebo vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
1,373 women were randomised in an outpatient setting in France.

Inclusion criteria: all nulliparous women at 41 0/7 weeks of gestation with intact membranes, a Bishop score less than 6, and a singleton fetus in cephalic presentation were eligible.

Exclusion criteria: age younger than 18 years, no social security coverage, indication for immediate labour induction, antihypertensive treatment, fetal death, or contraindications to isosorbide mononitrate treatment (known hypersensitivity to it, cardiovascular collapse, aortic stenosis, mitral stenosis, obstructive myocardial hypertrophy, systolic blood pressure less than 95 mmHg).
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the French Ministry of Health (Grant number AOM08169, P071212).

Char: Participants:
52 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Israel.
