Inclusion criteria: a singleton, term gestation (≥ 37 weeks), cephalic presentation, intact membranes, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score ≤ 6), presenting to our labour and delivery unit for labour induction secondary to oligohydramnios, defined as Amniotic Fluid Index ≤ 5 cm.

Exclusion criteria: women with a multifetal gestation, fetal malpresentation, spontaneous labour, contraindication to prostaglandins or a vaginal delivery (e.g., placenta previa), non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing, a fetus with major anomalies or previous caesarean delivery were excluded.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. Double balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was conducted without external funding.

Char: Participants:
245 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United Kingdom. 

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous and multiparous (but not more than para 5) women at term (37-42 completed weeks of gestation with ultrasound confirmed dates), with a singleton fetus of cephalic presentation, with medical or obstetric indications for the induction of labour were eligible to be included in the trial. A normal fetal heart tracing and a cervical Bishop score of less than 8 were also criteria for inclusion.

Exclusion criteria: women with previous uterine surgery, including a previous caesarean section, with significant fetal or medical concerns or known contraindications to the use of prostaglandins.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
100 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Scotland.

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous and multiparous (not more than para 5) women admitted to the Aberdeen Maternity Hospital (Aberdeen, Scotland) between the months of June and September 2000 for induction of labour for a medical or obstetric indication after 37 weeks of gestation. The other inclusion criteria were an unfavourable cervix (Bishop’s score less than 8) and a normal fetal heart tracing.

Exclusion criteria: multiple gestation or a presentation other than cephalic, previous caesarean delivery, known contraindications to the use of prostaglandins, and significant fetal or maternal concerns that made induction necessary under continuous monitoring.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
415 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Greece.

Inclusion criteria: (1) gestational age more than 37 weeks; (2) singleton pregnancy with vertex presentation; (3) intact membranes; (4) Bishop score ≤ 4; (5) reactive non-stress test; and (6) absence of labour.

Exclusion criteria: pregnant women were excluded due to the presence of at least one of the following conditions: (1) fetal malpresentation or other evidence of cephalopelvic disproportion; (2) suspected fetal distress (abnormal fetal heart rate patterns, oligohydramnios with Amniotic Fluid Index < 3, or severe intrauterine growth retardation); (3) placenta praevia or unexplained vaginal bleeding; (4) contraindication to prostaglandins administration (allergy, severe asthma or preexisting cardiac or cardiovascular disease); (5) renal or hepatic dysfunction; (6) previous caesarean delivery or uterine surgery; and (7) parity greater than five.
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Egypt.

Inclusion criteria: nulliparity, gestational age of at least 37 completed weeks, a singleton fetus with vertex presentation, unfavourable cervices (Bishop score < 6), intact membranes, reactive nonstress test, normal umbilical arterial Doppler indices, absence of labour, and willingness of women to participate in the study.

Exclusion criteria: multiparity, multiple pregnancy, fetal malpresentation, premature rupture of fetal membranes, regular uterine contractions, major cephalopelvic disproportion, and contraindications to isosorbide mononitrate (hypersensitivity to nitrates, hypotension, hypovolemia, cardiac disease, marked anaemia, and closed-angle glaucoma) or misoprostol [active cardiorespiratory disease, placenta previa, a history of caesarean delivery or major uterine surgery, and a nonreassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) pattern].
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Nitric oxide donors plus ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol (but this group was not included in this review)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
180 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sri Lanka.

Inclusion criteria: women who not delivered by 40 weeks + 5 days gestation with Modified Bishop Score (MBS) ≤ 5, having uncomplicated pregnancies with a singleton fetus, longitudinal lie and cephalic presentation.

Exclusion criteria: pregnancy-induced hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus, multiple pregnancies, planned caesarean section, fetal growth restriction and scarred uteri.
Char: Interventions: Single balloon catheter vs. < 50 µg oral misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
200 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Brazil.

Inclusion criteria: single live pregnancy, pregnancy duration of 37 weeks or more, indication for labour induction (hypertension, premature rupture of membranes, diabetes, or pregnancy duration of 41 weeks or more), vertex presentation, estimated fetal weight of less than 4000 g according to ultrasonography, amniotic fluid index of more than 5 cm, and modified Bishop score of 6 or less.

Exclusion criteria: women with uterine scar, abnormal fetal well-being test, fetal abnormalities, restricted fetal growth, genital bleeding related to placental abnormalities, or contraindications to vaginal delivery were excluded. Fetal well-being was evaluated by Doppler flow velocimetry, cardiotocography, and/or biophysical profile scoring, depending on the routine at each hospital.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
79 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Malaysia.

Inclusion criteria: one previous caesarean delivery, Bishop score of ≤ 5, age 18 years or older, term gestation (≥ 37 weeks), singleton fetus, cephalic presentation, intact membranes, and absence of ≥ 2 significant contractions in 10 min.

Exclusion criteria: women with known gross fetal anomaly, known allergy to any of the trial devices for induction, and inability to consent. Participants were excluded from this study if the cardiotocographic assessment was nonreassuring or Bishop score was ≥ 6.
Char: Interventions: Foley single balloon catheter vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Universiti Malaya.

Char: Participants:
100 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Switzerland.

Inclusion criteria: (1) willingness of the woman to participate in the study, (2) unfavourable cervix (Bishop score ≤ 5), (3) reactive nonstress test, (4) singleton with vertex presentation, and (5) absent labour.

Exclusion criteria: (1) fetal malpresentation, (2) history of caesarean section or uterine surgery, and (3) contraindication to receiving prostaglandins (allergy, severe asthma).
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
110 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Iran.

Inclusion criteria: gestation age greater than 37 weeks, Bishop score less than 4, singleton gestation, intact membranes, vertex presentation, no labour occurring and normal fetal heart rate.

Exclusion criteria: pelvic dystocia, evidence of cephalopelvic disproportion, placenta previa or any unexplained vaginal bleeding, fetal malformation, previous uterine scar and any situation when vaginal delivery was not indicated and any contraindication to the use of labour induction.
Char: Interventions: ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
171 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Singapore.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy, cephalic presentation, gestation greater than 37 completed weeks, no known contraindication to vaginal delivery, and modified Bishop score ≤ 6.

Exclusion criteria: previous caesarean section or other uterine surgery, significant maternal medical/obstetric complication in pregnancy (such as severe pre-eclampsia, significant antepartum haemorrhage), antepartum evidence of fetal compromise (such as fetal growth restriction), previous attempt at cervical priming and contraindication to receiving prostaglandins, including asthma and glaucoma.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) vs. ≥ 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from National Healthcare Group, Singapore (Grant number NHG-RPR/02004).

Char: Participants:
1,859 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the Netherlands.

Inclusion criteria: women with a vital singleton pregnancy in cephalic presentation, intact membranes, a gestational age of 37 weeks or more, and an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 6), scheduled for induction of labour.

Exclusion criteria: women with known hypersensitivity to any of the products used, age younger than 18 years, a history of caesarean section, placenta praevia, or a fetus known to have lethal congenital anomalies.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Single balloon catheter
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from FondsNutsOhra.

Char: Participants:
131 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Italy.

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy; fetal cephalic presentation; Bishop score ≤ 4; gestational age of 37–42 weeks; no previous caesarean section; intact membranes; maternal age ≥ 18 years.

Exclusion criteria: premature rupture of the membranes; history of a previous caesarean section; maternal clinical contraindications to the administration of prostaglandin E2 analogues; fetal malpresentation.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
170 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Thailand.

Inclusion criteria: term singleton pregnancy, premature rupture of membranes, cephalic presentation, parity less than 5, no history of hypersensitivity to prostaglandins, candidate for vaginal delivery, bishop scores ≤ 6 (unripped cervix), and no uterine scarring.

Exclusion criteria: abnormal fetal heart rate patterns, abnormal clinical pelvimetry and labour progression, prior uterine surgery, and refusal to participate in the study. Membranes were clinically confirmed by visualisation of pooling fluid in the posterior vaginal fornix through the cervix during sterile speculum examination.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg sublingual or buccal misoprostol vs. Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the Research Fund of Bhumibol Adulyadej Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand.

Char: Participants:
156 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sri Lanka.

Inclusion criteria: women with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies with cephalic presentations, and between 40 weeks + 5 days and 41 weeks’ gestation, where the dates had been confirmed by an early ultrasound scan, and having a cervix unfavourable for induction of labour with a modified Bishop Score < 5.

Exclusion criteria: women with any medical or obstetric problems and any contraindications for the use of isosorbide mononitrate.
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors vs. Nitric oxide donors vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: source(s) of funding for the study were not reported.

Char: Participants:
199 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Sweden.

Inclusion criteria: primiparous women with singleton gestations and cephalic presentation at ≥ 37 weeks of gestation and with a Bishop score of ≤ 4.

Exclusion criteria: an inability to understand the questionnaire written in Swedish, previous hysterotomy (scar in the uterine myometrium), and prenatal fetal complications such as intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) or non-reassuring cardiotocography (CTG) on admission (the ‘door test’ in the first 20 minutes of registration of CTG).
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. Controlled-release misoprostol vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: no funding was sought for this study.

Char: Participants:
206 women were randomised in a hospital setting in the United States.

Eligibility criteria: informed consent, singleton pregnancy of ≥ 37 weeks gestation, cephalic presentation, nulliparous or multiparous with ≤ 3 previous viable infants, a medical or obstetric indication for induction, bishop score of ≤ 4 on admission, reactive fetal nonstress test, no previous uterine scars, no vaginal bleeding, intact membranes, no fever of ≥ 38 °c, no allergy to prostaglandins, no history of asthma or glaucoma, except for childhood asthma without adult recurrences, no evidence of fetal distress, no evidence of spontaneous labour, no evidence of clinical hydramnios confirmed on ultrasonography, no use of aspirin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or acetaminophen within 4 h before insertion of pessary and anytime thereafter, no underlying maternal cardiac lesion that might put the patient at risk from potential hypotensive effects of prostaglandin E2, has not been administered a tocolytic or oxytocin within 24 hours of insertion of pessary
Char: Interventions: Placebo vs. Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from PharmaSciences, Inc.

Char: Participants:
511 women were randomised in a hospital setting in Canada.

Inclusion criteria: women were eligible if they presented at greater than 37 weeks gestation with an indication for induction, and a single live cephalic fetus.

Exclusion criteria: non-reassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) tracings, previous uterine surgery, known hypersensitivity to misoprostol or other prostaglandins, uncontrolled epilepsy or asthma, or contraindication to vaginal birth.
Char: Interventions: 50 µg oral misoprostol vs. < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from the IWK Health Centre, Research Services (Grant number 051.731.7303088).

Char: Participants:
225 women were randomised in a hospital setting in China.

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous women with a live singleton pregnancy who were eligible for induction labour were recruited in this study. All subjects were aged 20 years or older; had a gestational age between 37 and 42 weeks, with head fetal presentation and intact amniotic membrane. All subjects were induced labour for the indications according to the Chinese guideline of cervical ripening and labour induction during the third trimester of pregnancy but demonstrated an unfavourable cervix (cervical Bishop score ≤ 6).

Exclusion criteria: placenta previa, placenta abruption, breech or transverse presentation, significant cephalopelvic disproportion, preeclampsia or eclampsia, suspected macrosomia, emergent fetal distress, fetal congenital malformation, and prior uterine surgical procedure history. Women with severe chronic diseases of the cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematopoietic, endocrine, or immune system; acute infection; cervical carcinoma; and contraindications for the use of prostaglandin analogues (glaucoma, asthma, epilepsy, and allergy to prostaglandin) were also excluded.
Char: Interventions: < 50 µg vaginal misoprostol vs. Placebo
Char: Notes: Funding source: the study was supported by funding from Guangzhou Regenex Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Guangzhou, China.
